pages.commitMessage:
feat: retire the acting agents, silence their alarms, add the session brief

Three changes from one measurement: in six months the autonomous acting agents
changed src/ six times, while all 19 pages and every revenue-relevant change of
August came from human-directed sessions. The operating model is now explicit —
the pipeline observes, Jackson decides.

1. Wednesday/Thursday/Friday schedules retired to workflow_dispatch only. Not
for cost — they are ~$0.26/month between them — but because an idle acting
agent still files a stale-log finding every night, and an alarm that fires
because nothing happened is indistinguishable from one that fires because
something broke. Disabled, not deleted; the observation half all still runs and
is more valuable under this model, since it is the scoreboard for session work.

2. lib/retired-agents.ts. Disabling the cron ALONE would have made things worse:
the nightly loads fixes-log.md and content-log.md as contracted sources with a
192h SLA, so with their writers off it would have declared two contract failures
every night forever, for a condition that is now correct. The retirement is
recorded in two paired places — the cron and this file — and both say so, so
neither can be changed alone. Blind checks went 3 to 1.

3. scripts/session-brief.ts. If growth happens in sessions, the pipeline's job
is to make a session start at full context in seconds rather than twenty minutes
of re-gathering. Deterministic, no model call, $0. Leads with the active
kill-list constraints (a session proposing CTR work on a position-9.7 page has
wasted itself) and the conversion join of affiliate clicks x scroll depth x CTA
position — the hand-built version of which produced the 2026-08-28 placement
finding. Prints what it could not read rather than smoothing over it.

The brief's CTA column is a markup measure that overstates depth (45% there vs
13% rendered for aeron-size-c) and now carries that caveat in its own output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
